subject: art-therapy
intro: Art therapy leads into the activity-based allied health professions — where structured creative and recreational activity is planned, delivered and documented as treatment — and to rehabilitation counselling.

roles.title: Recreational Therapists
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate medically-approved recreation programs in hospitals, nursing homes and other institutions — including arts and crafts — assessing each patient's condition and recommending suitable therapeutic activity.
roles.where: The course's arc from assessment through treatment matches the role: media choices and responses, directive and non-directive delivery, and adapting creative activity for children, medical patients and older adults with dementia.

roles.title: Occupational Therapists
roles.what: Assess, plan and organise rehabilitative programs that build or restore vocational, homemaking and daily living skills for people with disabilities or developmental delays, adapting environments and specific tasks.
roles.where: The populations and settings unit — children and adolescents, medical art therapy, older adults — is OT caseload ground, and treatment approaches' goal-driven planning and cultural context of images inform patient-centred design.

roles.title: Rehabilitation Counselors
roles.what: Counsel people coping with personal, social and vocational difficulties from illness, injury, aging or disability, assessing client needs and designing rehabilitation programs that maximise independence and employability.
roles.where: The profession unit's credentials, supervision and ethics standards, and the assessment unit's honest look at its own limits, train the counselling stance: client strengths, boundaries and evidence-based practice.
